Data table

toolkit::datatable draws tabular data: a header of sortable, resizable columns over virtualised one-line rows, with a pager footer. It is built on egui_extras' table for layout, scrolling and column resizing, and it follows the engine-first rule of the egui applications decision: the table only reports what the person did, and the app decides what that means.

The first user is Email's message list, which sorts and pages on the server. The source is libs/toolkit/src/datatable.rs and its engine, datatable/model.rs.

The pieces

PieceWhat it is
Columnid, Fluent label key, Width, Align, sortable (with the first click's Order), elide
WidthFixed(pt), Resizable { initial, min }, Share { share, min } (a fraction of the table, resizable), Remainder { min }
Rowsthe shown page: len, key(row), cell(row, column), optional style(row) and custom(ui, row, column)
Celltext, marker icons drawn at the cell's end, weak
RowStylestrong (the medium face, for unread mail), weak
TextRowsrows held as cells, for tests and small tables
TableStatesort, page, page size, selection (row keys), focus, dragged widths, density; serialisable
TableEventSortChanged, PageChanged, PageSizeChanged, Selected, Activated, ColumnResized
TotalKnown(n), or Unknown { more } when the size of the set is not known
DataTablethe widget: DataTable::new(id, &columns, &state), its options, then .show(ui, &rows)

Using it

use toolkit::datatable::{Column, DataTable, Order, TableState, Total, Width, Align};

let columns = vec![
    Column::new("name", "column-name")
        .width(Width::Share { share: 0.3, min: 80.0 })
        .sortable(Order::Ascending),
    Column::new("detail", "column-detail").width(Width::Remainder { min: 120.0 }),
    Column::new("size", "column-size")
        .width(Width::Fixed(72.0))
        .align(Align::End)
        .sortable(Order::Descending),
];

// each frame, from the app's state:
let events = DataTable::new("files", &columns, &state.table)
    .total(Total::Known(state.total))
    .strings(&strings)
    .page_sizes(&[50, 100, 200])
    .empty_text(strings.get("empty"))
    .show(ui, &rows);
for event in events {
    state.table.apply(&event, SelectionMode::Single);
    // then: re-sort in memory, or ask the server for the new page
}

Drawing never changes the app's state: show returns events, and the app applies them after the frame, like every other view event.

Sorting and paging

A header click on a sortable column reports SortChanged: another column starts in its first order (a date's newest first), the sorted column reverses, and with allow_unsorted(true) a third click goes back to no sort. A sort or page change moves the page back to the first.

The table never reorders or slices rows itself. An app holding every row in memory uses sort_rows(&mut rows, state.sort.as_ref(), compare) (a stable sort; compare_text folds case) and page_of(&rows, &state). An app whose rows live on a server sends the sort and state.offset() with its query, and keeps only the newest answer.

The footer shows "x–y of N" (or "x–y" for an unknown total), the optional page size picker, and first, previous, next and last. TableState::can and page_event answer the same questions for commands, so an app's "Next Page" menu entry and its footer button agree.

Rows, selection and the keyboard

Rows are one line at the design's row height: the chrome's menu-row height in Density::Compact, an item gap more above and below in Comfortable. Long cells are cut to the column with "…" and show the whole text in a tooltip.

A click selects a row (Ctrl-click toggles one in SelectionMode::Multi), a double-click activates it, and the click gives the table the keyboard. Then Up, Down, Page Up, Page Down, Home and End move the selection and scroll it into view, and Enter activates it. The selection is held as row keys, so TableState::rows_changed(&keys) keeps it across a refresh and drops what is gone.

Context menus and focus

.context_menu(&mut |ui, row| …) gives rows a right-click menu. A right-click on a row outside the selection selects it first (Selected), then reports ContextMenu { index, key } and opens a popup that the closure fills. Apps fill it from their command registry with Registry::context_menu(ui, state, strings, &ids, &why), which draws the commands ids with their labels, shortcuts, ticks and enablement, and returns the one chosen for the app to run with Origin::Menu. Registry::ids_in(menu) lists a menu's commands.

datatable::is_focused(ctx, id) says whether the table has the keyboard, and datatable::focus(ctx, id) gives it the keyboard. Focus-scoped shortcuts, such as single keys that must never fire in a text field, use these.

Dragging rows

.draggable(&|count| label) makes rows a drag source. A drag that starts on a selected row carries the whole selection, in page order. One that starts on an unselected row selects that row and carries it alone. The table reports DragStarted { keys }, puts a RowsDrag { table, keys } payload on egui's DragAndDrop, and shows label(count), for example "3 messages", in a badge by the pointer. A drop target reads the payload with DragAndDrop::payload::<RowsDrag>(ctx), checks table, and takes it on release. Email's folder tree works this way. Agents never drag: the app's own verb, email.move in Email, takes the same state path.

Columns shown and density

TableState::hidden holds the columns the person hid. ColumnShown toggles one, and DensityChanged switches between compact and comfortable. Both are preferences, so an app keeps them with the widths.

Widths and persistence

TableState is one serialisable struct. Persist the parts that are a preference (sort, widths, density) in the app's config, and keep the page and selection for the session. A dragged column reports ColumnResized once the drag ends; the next launch starts the column at that width.

Agents

The table is an AccessKit Table node labelled with its target id. Each row is a Row node labelled with its cells' text, comma separated, and marked selected; each header is a button carrying its sort direction; the pager's buttons are labelled "First page", "Previous page", "Next page" and "Last page". So the drive verbs work on it as a hand does:

send email email.ui.tree role="Row"
send email email.ui.click label="Subject"
send email email.ui.click label="Next page"

The table verbs

Every table can be read and driven through the Bus with no extra app code. toolkit::datatable::verbs is a standard verb set that an app mounts under its own prefix:

VerbArgumentsDoes
<app>.table.state—columns (id, label key, sortable, width, visible), sort, order, page, page size, pages, total, range, selection, focus, density and the shown rows
<app>.table.sortcolumn, optional order (asc/desc)sorts, as a header click does
<app>.table.pageindex (0-based, or first/previous/next/last)shows a page
<app>.table.page_sizensets the page size
<app>.table.selectrows (keys or indices)selects rows, the first replacing the selection
<app>.table.activaterowactivates a row, as Enter or a double-click does
<app>.table.contextrowselects a row for its context menu (the menu's commands run through <app>.execute)
<app>.table.columnid, optional width and visibleresizes, shows or hides a column
<app>.table.densitycompact or comfortablesets the row height

To mount the set:

  1. List verbs::describe(app) in the app's app.describe.
  2. Register the names in verbs.conf.mix, with table.state as a query and the rest as intents.
  3. When one arrives, call verbs::request(verb, args, &verbs::Table { columns, state, total, keys, allow_unsorted }). It checks the arguments against the table. It returns either Request::State or Request::Events(events), which are the same TableEvents a person's clicks raise. A bad argument is refused as Refusal::Invalid or Refusal::NotFound.
  4. Apply the events through the path the UI's events take, then answer with TableState::describe plus rows_json.

verbs::verb_for(&event) names the verb for each event, so an app's registry test can check that every event its table raises has a verb. Email mounts the set as email.table.* for its message list. There table.page_size is refused, because the page size is the email.mail.page_size setting.

Tests

The engine's rules (sort cycling, page arithmetic, keyboard moves, selection clamping, the client-side helpers) are unit tests in datatable/model.rs. libs/toolkit/tests/datatable.rs drives a sample table through kittest (header sorts, row selection and keys, double-click, the pager, an empty page) and snapshots it in Pro light and Studio dark.
